dataset.name: Arctic delta Landsat image classifications
description: This dataset contains binary geotiff masks/classifications of six Arctic deltas for channels, lakes, land, and other small water bodies (see methods). Tiff files can be opened with any image viewer, but use of georeferencing data attached to the imagery will require a GIS platform (e.g., QGIS). Dataset includes individually classified scene masks for Colville (2014), Kolyma (2014), Lena (2016), Mackenzie (2014), Yenisei (2013), and Yukon (2014). We also provide .mat files for each delta that include a 2D array of the mosaicked images that is cropped to include only the area used in our analyses (see Piliouras and Rowland, 2020, Journal of Geophysical Research - Earth Surface), as well as the X (easting) and Y (northing) arrays for georeferencing, with coordinates in UTMs.

citation: Piliouras, A., and J. C. Rowland. (2020). Arctic River Delta Morphologic Variability and Implications for Riverine Fluxes to the Coast. Journal of Geophysical Research - Earth Surface, 125, e2019JF005250. https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JF005250.
measurementTechnique: This dataset contains image classification masks (geotiffs) of Landsat 8 scenes, covering six high-latitude deltas: Colville (2014), Kolyma (2014), Lena (2016), Mackenzie (2014), Yenisei (2013), and Yukon (2014). Years were selected to obtain a modern day image with as little cloud-cover as possible, and all classifications were made on late summer imagery. Scenes were classified using eCognition. Here we provide the individually classified scene masks, as opposed to the mosaicked scenes. Each scene was classified into land, channels, lakes, and other “small water” (objects <= 4 pixels in width). Some scenes were cropped to remove cloud-covered areas, minimize overlap between scenes to be mosaicked, and/or exclude non-delta regions. For each classified Landsat scene, we provide 4 binary masks: channels, lakes, land, and small water. Files are named with the following convention, using the Yukon as an example, “Yukon2014_156010_210_lakes.tif,” where Yukon is the delta name, 2014 is the year of the image, 156 is the Landsat scene path, 010 is the Landsat scene row, 210 is the Julian date, and “lakes” indicates it is the lakes mask. Matlab files for each delta include a 2D array of the mosaicked images (0 = not in analysis, 1 = channels, 2 = lakes, 3 = small water, 4 = land) that is cropped to include only the area used in our analyses, as well as the X (easting) and Y (northing) arrays for georeferencing, with coordinates in UTMs. A more thorough description of classification methods can be found in: Piliouras A., & J. C. Rowland, (2019), Morphologic variability of Arctic deltas and the potential implications for fluxes to the coast, Marine Geology.
